subject.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor this durable-core architecture and restack it for a post-2026.7.1 release, or narrow recovery work to the existing restart/session-delivery primitives?
rationale: The branch introduces a new shared runtime, persisted data model, protocol surface, operational environment controls, and recovery semantics; code review cannot choose that permanent product boundary or release sequence.

options.title: Sponsor and restack
options.body: Adopt the architecture, retarget a clean ordered stack to the maintainer-selected branch, and require the identified proof and dependency fixes before landing.

options.title: Narrow the recovery scope
options.body: Keep the existing restart and session-delivery architecture, extracting only the smallest recovery primitives needed for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57425.

options.title: Pause the durable stack
options.body: Close or pause the stack until a maintainer-authored durable-runtime design and release plan exists.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and restack
recommendation.body: Adopt the architecture, retarget a clean ordered stack to the maintainer-selected branch, and require the identified proof and dependency fixes before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent Gateway lifecycle and session-delivery work makes them the best available routing candidate for the architecture and sequencing decision.
